name: How should a backsplash end at the side of a cabinet or open wall?

mainEntity.name: How should a backsplash end at the side of a cabinet or open wall?

acceptedAnswer.text:
**Direct answer:** The best edge treatment depends on whether the backsplash ends at a wall, cabinet, window, appliance, or open area. Options may include finished tile edges, trim pieces, a planned return, or a clean transition to another surface.

**Context:** An exposed raw tile edge can make a finished backsplash look incomplete, especially in open kitchens or at the end of a cabinet run. Edge details should be decided before tile is ordered because trim dimensions affect layout.

**Key factors:**
- Identify every exposed side and top edge.
- Match trim finish to cabinet hardware, appliances, or other metal details when appropriate.
- Confirm how corners and window returns will be handled.

**Practical guidance:** Mark stopping points on the elevation and request a sample of the proposed trim or edge finish. Do not assume the installer will choose an edge detail without approval.

**Soft positioning:** Elite Remodeling & Design can resolve edge details during design development before installation begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use a finished tile edge, trim, return, or planned transition based on the stopping point and surrounding materials. Identify every exposed side, top, window return, and corner before ordering tile. Approve the edge sample and layout so raw cuts are not left visible.
